# Feature: Push block — sanity check

<!-- Generated by the project-manager tool from pm.yml. Do not edit by hand; the store is the source of truth. -->

## Goal

Sanity-check candidate mechanic #81 (Push block) from Blocks before it is used in real levels. Effect: Push onto floor or a switch to hold it; it cannot enter hazards. Unique: the plain movable block; filling or cancelling hazards belongs to the dirt block (90) and ice block (82). Useful: holds buttons and blocks enemies; it does not cover hazards. Source status in the candidate file is 'revised'; it was revised from human review and is now treated as a trial candidate.

## User Story

**As a** player

**I want** push onto floor or a switch to hold it; it cannot enter hazards.

**So that** holds buttons and blocks enemies; it does not cover hazards.

## High-Level Use Case

The player meets Push block for the first time in its teaching room (mech-81-push-block-room). Teaching moment: First room: one block, a switch across the room, and open wall space behind the block. A player who pushes it in the first direction that moves it usually corners it against a wall, where it cannot be pulled back, so the switch can never be held and the small room must be restarted, which teaches that a push is chosen by its destination. The sanity check plays that room, exercises every rule below, and records a replayable session.

## Player-Facing Behavior

- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Press toward the block and it moves one tile only if the tile beyond is empty floor or a switch plate (floor switch 21 or weight switch 29)
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: It cannot be pulled
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Walls, locks, closed gates, other blocks and enemies block the push: the block and you both stay
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Water, deep water, void, fire and lava also block the push: the block never enters or covers them
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: On a switch plate it holds that switch down for as long as it sits there
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: It occupies its tile, so enemies cannot move through it

## Edge Cases & Rules

- Press toward the block and it moves one tile only if the tile beyond is empty floor or a switch plate (floor switch 21 or weight switch 29)
- It cannot be pulled
- Walls, locks, closed gates, other blocks and enemies block the push: the block and you both stay
- Water, deep water, void, fire and lava also block the push: the block never enters or covers them
- It occupies its tile, so enemies cannot move through it
- Movement/state stays deterministic: state advances only through the pure step function with recorded t_ms; a recorded session replays to the same end state.
- Restart (R / restart) restores the room to its initial state, including this mechanic.

## UI / Feedback

- The player sees Push block's effect happen on its tile(s) exactly as the rules above describe; no hidden state.
- Any counter, inventory or HUD impact follows the rules above; if a rule needs a counter it is shown while it matters (see Open Questions).
- Failure in the teaching room returns the player to the room start / checkpoint for an immediate retry.
